known_facts_book1: A Munchkin magician so crooked in body that his legs are as handy as his arms, living high on the mountain between the Munchkin and Gillikin Countries with his wife Margolotte.
Is the only person in the world who knows how to make the Powder of Life, which takes six years of stirring four kettles with both hands and both feet.
Gave his first batch of the Powder of Life to old Mombi the Witch, receiving in exchange a worthless Powder of Perpetual Youth.
Invented the Liquid of Petrifaction, which turns whatever it touches to solid marble, and used it on two Kalidahs he keeps as garden statuary.
Made the Glass Cat with pink brains and a ruby heart, and admits she was a bungle.
Is forbidden by Ozma's Law to practice magic, and claims the right to work it only for his own family.
Sprinkles the Powder of Life on the Patchwork Girl; her flung arm knocks the bottle away and the spilled Liquid of Petrifaction turns his wife and Unc Nunkie to marble.
Names the five ingredients of the compound that would undo the Liquid of Petrifaction, reading them from a small blue-leather Book of Recipes.
Is brought to the palace by Ozma, who destroys his four kettles and burns his book of recipes.
Is stripped of all magic power by the Wizard, who at the same stroke straightens every crooked limb, leaving him a simple Munchkin and no longer crooked.

known_relations_book1.Margolotte: His wife, whom he petrifies by accident and mourns as lost forever.
known_relations_book1.Unc Nunkie: An old friend of many years, petrified in the same accident.

known_relations_book1.Scraps: The Patchwork Girl he brings to life with the Powder of Life.
known_relations_book1.Bungle: The Glass Cat he made and regrets making.
known_relations_book1.the Wizard: Deprives him of his magic power by royal edict, and straightens his body.
known_relations_book1.Ozma: The Ruler whose Law forbids his magic and who orders his powers taken away.

known_facts_book1: The chubby, pleasant-faced wife of Dr. Pipt, dressed all in blue, an excellent cook who welcomes strangers to her lonely mountain house.
Names her visitors on sight: Unc Nunkie the Silent One, and Ojo the Unlucky.
Sewed the Patchwork Girl out of her grandmother's hundred-year-old patchwork quilt, to have a servant for the housework.
Deliberately gave the girl a face of mismatched patches and a body of unpopular colors so she could never be proud or rebellious.
Chose only 'Obedience', 'Amiability' and 'Truth' from the Brain Furniture shelf, plus a little 'Cleverness' at Unc Nunkie's suggestion, meaning the servant's brains not to be very good.
Had intended to name the Patchwork Girl 'Angeline'.
Is turned to marble by the spilled Liquid of Petrifaction, standing beside Unc Nunkie in the workshop.
Is restored to life by the Wizard and runs at once into her husband's arms.

known_relations_book1.Dr. Pipt: Her husband, who makes the Powder of Life for her and mourns her petrification.
known_relations_book1.Scraps: The Patchwork Girl she made and stuffed and meant to keep as a servant.
known_relations_book1.Bungle: The Glass Cat she named 'Bungle' and who refuses to catch mice for her.
known_relations_book1.Ojo: The boy she feeds and nicknames, and who journeys to restore her.
known_relations_book1.the Wizard: Restores her to life with Glinda's method.
